ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, managers, and authorized signatories against EU consolidated sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated lists, OFAC SDN List, Luxembourg national sanctions orders, PEP databases, and adverse media/regulatory sanctions. Continuous screening throughout the corporate life and enhanced due diligence triggered by any PEP, negative-media, or sanctions hit; protocols aligned with CSSF Regulation 19-05 and the amended LAML/CFT regime.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) e-portal, www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name may be based on French, German, Luxembourgish, or another Latin-script language. Non-Latin scripts are permitted only with a mandatory transliteration into Latin characters. The SCSp name must end with the legal form suffix 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The name must be distinctive and not identical or confusingly similar to any existing RCS registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: TIR requiring concession from the road-transport licensing authority
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the LBR/RCS rejects the name, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request to the RCS within 5 business days from notification. If recollection is refused or the rejection is maintained, the applicant may lodge a formal administrative appeal with the Tribunal administratif of Luxembourg within 3 months from the date of notification. Legal representation by an avocat admitted to the Luxembourg Bar is mandatory for the administrative appeal. The applicant may simultaneously resubmit a new name reservation request with a newly proposed distinctive name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is tolerated by the RCS when operated by an LBR-certified registered agent and used solely for the legal seat address. However, for an active long-haul TIR freight enterprise, a pure virtual office without a physical operating base in Luxembourg will fail statutory and prudent commercial-substance tests under Luxembourg customs, transport-licensing, social security, and tax rules. The SCSp should maintain a physical operating and fleet-administration centre in Luxembourg for staff, vehicles, and regulatory compliance files.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High, approximately 70% probability of unannounced on-site inspection during the first year of TIR operations by the Luxembourg road-transport inspectorate and customs authorities, given the sector's regulatory sensitivity and obligations under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 and the Luxembourg law of 22 June 1996 concerning road transport.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101-1 to 101-26 (SCSp regime as inserted by the Law of 12 July 2013); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) and RESA; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on RCS filing procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operating the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 2, avenue du Blues, L-4368 Esch-sur-Alzette, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS Form C (formulaire C) accompanied by the executed SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société), manager acceptance and specimen signature, registered-office consent, and filing fee receipt; filed electronically via lbr.lu
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital: the SCSp's capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement. Contributions may be in cash, in kind, or in industry (general partner only); no escrow account or bank certificate is required under Luxembourg company law, but the manager must record each contribution in the partnership's capital register and the subscribed funds must be made available to the partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned partners ratify the subscription of partnership capital as set out in the Contribution Register, such capital being fully credited to the SCSp's capital accounts. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Société en Commandite Spéciale be fixed at [address], Luxembourg, where the effective administration is located. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be appointed Manager (Gérant), acting singly, with full authority to represent the partnership, open bank accounts, execute TIR Carnet guarantee agreements, and complete all statutory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Manager be authorized to file these resolutions with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and to sign all related documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (mandatory for real-property contributions) and licensed corporate counsel; Guichet.lu electronic template for standard private deeds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (contrat de société) setting out the corporate name, Luxembourg registered office, contribution schedule, capital account mechanics, distribution waterfall, and identification of the general partner (associé commandité) and limited partners (associés commanditaires). Execute by private written deed or, where contributions comprise immovable property, by notarial act. Each partner signs personally or under power of attorney; the manager files a written acceptance of appointment.
required_dossiers: Certified passport/ID copies of all partners
Proof of residential/business address of each partner
Proxy powers of attorney where signing by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel issues an AML or document query, provide supplementary sworn declarations and bank references within 10 business days; the deed may be re-executed without loss of filing priority once the file is complete.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed RCS Form C together with the executed partnership agreement (or a certified extract where partner confidentiality is elected), manager appointment acceptance with specimen signature, and the registered-office consent. File via the LBR e-filing portal at lbr.lu or at the RCS single desk. Pay the statutory EUR 75 registration fee. The RCS issues the registration extract and assigns the RCS number.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (or certified confidential extract)
Registered-office address consent from premises owner
Proof of payment of the EUR 75 filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a request for further information, respond with corrected filings within 15 business days; non-response results in rejection, after which a fresh application with corrected particulars and a new fee receipt must be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of statutory particulars in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of RCS registration, file the mandatory statutory particulars (name, registered office, object, manager identity, capital, RCS number) for electronic publication in RESA. Where the partnership agreement is confidential, publish only the legal particulars. The RESA publication extract serves as presumptive proof against third parties and is required for subsequent tax and bank filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA request is returned for incomplete metadata, correct and re-file within 5 business days via the LBR portal; publication is accepted automatically once the data match the RCS extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration — VAT, direct tax, and excise formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration des douanes et accises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration application with the AEDT (via myGuichet.lu), attaching the RCS extract and RESA publication; obtain the Luxembourg VAT number required for intra-EU TIR transports, input VAT recovery on fuel, tolls and vehicle leases, and intrastat declarations. Register the pass-through partnership with the ACD for the issuance of the Luxembourg tax residence certificate. Notify the customs and excise administration if commercial bonded fuel tanks are maintained.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT returns a completeness query, resubmit through myGuichet.lu within 15 business days; voluntary correction of an inadvertent omission mitigates administrative fines otherwise imposed for late registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income tax and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; consolidated filings via MyGuichet.lu and eC.A.T.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-registered SCSp obtains a national identification number (NID) automatically upon RCS registration. For VAT, the SCSp must file form 3 (VAT registration) with the AEDT, submit its commercial registry extract and articles of association, and identify its partners/activities. Non-resident partners must provide their foreign VAT/TIN identifiers; the VAT number is issued electronically through eC.A.T within 3-5 weeks.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box system in Luxembourg; SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent. For VAT, the transparent partnership may elect to be treated as an independent taxable person for activities carried out in its own name. Hybrid mismatch rules require aligned elections with foreign counterparty classifications under EU ATAD 2016/1164 provisions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover for domestic exemption; no threshold for non-resident suppliers or importers to register (mandatory registration regardless of turnover when acquiring intra-EU goods or providing B2C digital services).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G e-invoicing is mandatory in Peppol/UBL formats; B2B e-invoicing is not yet mandatory. No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping exists. VAT returns and lists, including EC Sales Lists, must be filed via eC.A.T.; e-invoices must be retained for 6 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods outside the EU under customs procedures, including TIR transit, are zero-rated when ownership transfers to a non-EU customer and transport outside the EU is evidenced. International transport of goods from Luxembourg to non-EU destinations and linked loading/unloading services are zero-rated if covered by a CMR/TIR Carnet and the service is directly linked to the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EX-A and NCTS TIR electronic declaration)
Bill of Lading / CMR Consignment Note
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing foreign-currency proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating triggers retroactive VAT collection plus late interest at 5% per year (or higher), fines up to EUR 500,000, administrative sanctions, seizure of goods/vehicles, and criminal prosecution for VAT fraud under articles 51-53 of the Luxembourg VAT law; the tax authorities may apply joint liability to the SCSp and its partners where zero-rating is abused.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem; banking conduct, AML/CFT supervision, and payment institution licensing are supervised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg does not maintain a separate foreign-exchange administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg maintains unrestricted free movement of capital and payments under Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and imposes no foreign-exchange controls, conversion licensing, or central bank approval for current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance is commercially available through normal bank transfers; for an SCSp, distributions are treated as partnership withdrawals rather than taxable dividends because the entity is fiscally transparent, and no Luxembourg withholding tax is levied on such distributions. Remittance is nevertheless subject to standard anti-abuse, documentation, and EU/CFSP sanctions screening requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg has no statutory obligation to surrender, convert, or repatriate export receipts within a mandatory timeline. TIR carnet revenues may be credited directly and in full to the SCSp's euro treasury account. The only relevant customs obligation is the orderly discharge of the TIR carnet within the prescribed transit deadlines through the national guaranteeing chain.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
Société Générale Bank & Trust Luxembourg S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low for an unlicensed offshore digital EMI; Medium-to-High for an EEA-authorised e-money institution or payment institution that has completed a PSD2 passport notification with the CSSF. Legal constraints: only a licensed credit institution, e-money institution, or payment institution may issue electronic money, hold commercial payment accounts, or initiate SEPA and SWIFT MT103 transactions. An offshore EMI without an EU passport cannot lawfully provide Luxembourg IBANs or process treasury payments; sub-licensing is prohibited, and any arrangement using unregulated payment intermediaries would fail AML/CFT due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, a first-time non-resident SCSp is expected to provide at least one physical interview for the natural-person ultimate beneficial owner or for the general partner's managing director; a Luxembourg-resident professional director may satisfy this requirement where the bank has adequate client acceptance. Remote onboarding is possible only under a CSSF-compliant video-identification process for EEA-resident individuals and, in many banks, only where an existing EU banking group relationship exists. For non-EEA beneficial owners or complex partnership chains, banks generally require notarised and apostilled constitutional documents plus physical attendance or a personal visit to a Luxembourg branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp presented as an unfunded or zero-capital partnership with a non-resident corporate general partner and limited Luxembourg substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed partnership agreement, RCS/RCSC excerpt, registered office or professional agent agreement in Luxembourg, capital contribution records, detailed TIR trucking business plan, and a written substance memorandum demonstrating management, banking, invoicing, and control functions in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial-ownership chain through multiple intermediate entities or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Entity structure chart, certified passport copies, signed UBO declarations for all natural persons, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, confirmation that no nominee structures are used, and independent sanctions screening reports covering all partners, directors, and principal counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trucking revenue pattern with numerous small cash-like transactions, fuel-card payments, and sub-contractor payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements with cargo owners, CMR waybills, TIR carnet customs files, fuel-card monthly statements and transaction logs, subcontractor due-diligence packs, expected monthly transaction volumes and values, and a clear explanation of the payment rails used for each counterparty class.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear tax classification or undocumented profit-sharing ratios in the SCSp agreement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax classification confirmation or advance tax ruling, partnership agreement profit/loss allocation clauses, capital account statements, and an independent accountant's report confirming the SCSp's fiscally transparent treatment and the legal basis for partner distributions.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use an SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR funding or a SWIFT MT103/MT202 for non-EUR funding from the investor's regulated bank into the SCSp's Luxembourg IBAN. Use ISO 20022 purpose code CAPT (Capital Payment) and remittance reference 'SCSp capital contribution – TIR/LU_SCSP'. For non-EUR transfers, execute an explicit FX spot or forward with the receiving bank before remittance. The receiving bank may require the partnership agreement, UBO declarations, and a record of contributing partners to satisfy CSSF AML duties. Cash, crypto, and third-party or unlicensed payment intermediaries must never be used for capital injections.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer for routine supplier, subcontractor, and operational payments; use irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued under ICC UCP600 for large rolling-stock and equipment purchases, with reimbursement through SWIFT MT202 COV. Fuel and toll payments are cleared through established fuel-card networks such as DKV, UTA, and Shell Card, generally with SEPA B2B direct debit. TIR carnet liabilities are discharged through the recognised Luxembourg guaranteeing association. Every disbursement is matched to the underlying invoice, CMR transport document, and TIR carnet record to maintain audit trail and AML defence.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts for EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, and corridor currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible corridor currencies
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term treasury rebalancing
European-style plain-vanilla FX options for contingency exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO confirmation (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RCS UBO Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based annual confirmation as set by the LBR electronic reminder; amended UBO declaration required within 30 days after any change in ownership or beneficial interest.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties up to EUR 125,000 for legal persons and EUR 10,000 for natural persons, plus daily penalty of up to EUR 100 per day of delay; wilful omission may attract criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts deposit and RCS publication (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 7 months after the financial year-end, e.g., by 31 July for a 31 December fiscal year-end, unless the SCSp benefits from a filing exemption.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of EUR 1,000–5,000, possible court order to compel filing, and prolonged non-filing exposes the SCSp to judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory register audit and certification of partners register, manager register, minute book, and UBO register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Maintained at the registered office; produced to the RCS, court, or supervisory authority upon demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited and certified at each annual partners' meeting, normally within 2 months of financial year-end, and continuously updated within 30 days of any partner or manager change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain statutory registers constitutes an AML/company-law violation carrying fines up to EUR 250,000 and potential disqualification of the general partner.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for the SCSp if it exceeds two of the three following thresholds: balance sheet total of EUR 6,250,000; net turnover of EUR 12,500,000; average workforce of 50 employees in a fiscal year. Audit is also required under special AML or financial-sector regulations or when validly requested by partners representing at least 10% of partnership interests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2008 on annual and consolidated accounts; IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements where applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must file and maintain an accurate UBO declaration with the Luxembourg Business Registers. The declaration must be confirmed annually on the LBR-assigned anniversary date. Any transfer or change in partnership interests that affects beneficial ownership must be reported through an amended UBO declaration within 30 days, and the partner register must be updated contemporaneously. The annual confirmation is performed electronically through the RCS e-file portal.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of managers / general partner appointments
Minute book of partners' general and special resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 - 4,000 per annum (Luxembourg registered office and domiciliation agent)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 20,000 per annum (approved Luxembourg statutory auditor / réviseur d'entreprises)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City rate for an ordinary Luxembourg corporate taxpayer, comprising 17% corporate income tax, 7% unemployment surcharge on that CIT, and 6.75% municipal business tax. A Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent: the SCSp itself is not liable to Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax; partners are taxable on their distributable shares. A foreign corporate partner with a Luxembourg permanent establishment pays Luxembourg CIT on the PE-attributable profit at the normal aggregate rate.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is pass-through and therefore has no entity-level CIT holiday. Taxable partners may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption on qualified dividends and capital gains), the IP Box tax regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income), the notional interest deduction, and DTA relief. No withholding tax applies to interest or royalties paid by a Luxembourg payer. Loss carryforward is unlimited at the partner level under Art. 110 LIR, subject to anti-abuse rules on change of business and greater-than-50% shareholding change.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited at the taxable partner level; no entity-level limitation for a transparent SCSp.
